A 7-year-old boy presents to the emergency department after an episode of jerking his extremities followed by confusion.
The mother states this episode lasted about 3 minutes and involved full-body jerking.
This has happened in the past, but his mother thought he was fabricating his symptoms.
The child has a history of migraine headaches with aura that resolve with ibuprofen.
The patient is protecting his airway but is unable to answer questions.
After the episode, the child was non-responsive but was breathing on his own.
He is able to move the right upper and lower extremity.
He has had an MRI of the brain with no acute findings in the past.
He is otherwise healthy and has no medical problems or recent illness and is up to date on his vaccinations.
The mother notes that this is similar to his past episodes.
